authority.legal_name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA)
authority.geography_type: island city-state with a busy harbour, southern islands, and two cross-border water surfaces
authority.home_waters_label: Singapore's harbour, the Southern Islands and the inner waterfront

mandate.summary: MPA regulates and develops the Port of Singapore — the world's busiest transshipment hub — and stewards the harbour-craft fleet's transition to clean energy. Its remit covers harbour-craft licensing, berth and charging infrastructure, vessel standards, and the decarbonization of domestic marine transport.
current_priorities: Decarbonize the domestic harbour-craft fleet (electrification + cleaner fuels)
Set vessel reference designs and standards for clean harbour craft
Deliver the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint 2050

policy_targets.harbour_craft_mandate: From 2030, all new harbour craft operating in the Port of Singapore must be fully electric, capable of using B100 biofuel, or compatible with net-zero fuels.
policy_targets.net_zero_scope: Net-zero harbour craft (and pleasure craft) by 2050; national net-zero by 2050.
policy_targets.relevance: Foiling makes the electric option fast and practical — the credible way to meet the 2030 mandate without compromising speed or range. MPA can prove it first-of-class at home and export the standard.

precedent.headline: Singapore has already mandated clean harbour craft — and is building the charging to run them.

harbour_craft_electrification.rule: All new harbour craft fully electric / B100-capable / net-zero-fuel compatible from 2030; net-zero harbour craft by 2050.
harbour_craft_electrification.charging_pilot: First e-HC charging point launched at Marina South Pier (Pyxis + SP Mobility, 2024); national e-HC charging masterplan and standards in development.
harbour_craft_electrification.designs: 11 passenger-launch and cargo-lighter e-HC vessel designs shortlisted (2024); reference designs being developed with research institutes.
harbour_craft_electrification.financing: MPA EOIs for e-HC financing and insurance show strong institutional interest; premiums comparable to conventional craft.
harbour_craft_electrification.key_fact_for_navier: MPA has mandated clean harbour craft, built the first charging point, and is selecting reference vessel designs. A foiling vessel is the fast, premium, exportable option that fits the mandate from day one.
harbour_craft_electrification.fleet_size: ~1,600 diesel harbour craft to transition (up to ~2,000 vessels ply port waters).
harbour_craft_electrification.notification_rule: Operators with new harbour-craft plans must inform MPA from January 2027 so designs can be adjusted (MPA EOI, Jul 2023).

causeway.stat: ~350,000 crossings per day — one of the busiest land border crossings in the world; long peak queues.
causeway.rts_link: The Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link (Bukit Chagar <-> Woodlands North) opens end-2026 to ease Causeway congestion.
causeway.relevance: A fast cross-border marine link offers Causeway-peak relief — a recognized public-good framing. Secondary to the domestic harbour network.

domestic_ferries_today.southern_islands: Marina South Pier (MRT NS28) is the gateway: Singapore Island Cruise & Ferry Services and Marina South Ferries run daily island-hopping to St John's, Lazarus, Kusu and Sisters' Islands; Marina South Ferries also sails Sentosa Jetty @ Cove (Sentosa Cove Village) <-> Lazarus in ~15 min.
domestic_ferries_today.pulau_ubin: Changi Point Ferry Terminal <-> Pulau Ubin: 12-passenger bumboats, ~10 min, S$4-5 cash per leg, depart when full. Pulau Ubin draws ~300,000 visitors a year (NParks).
domestic_ferries_today.relevance: Domestic water transport already exists on slow displacement craft — a foiling upgrade is an improvement to a live mode, not a novelty.
domestic_ferries_today.kusu_pilgrimage: Annual Kusu Pilgrimage Season (Ninth Lunar Month, e.g. 21 Oct-19 Nov 2025): appointed operator runs hourly departures 7am-4pm from Marina South Pier; capacity-managed in peak years (50 pax/hour caps).
domestic_ferries_today.jetty_renewal: St John's Island jetty and Kusu bumboat jetty closed 24 Apr 2025, extended to 23 Mar 2026, for repair; ferries rerouted to Lazarus Pulau Seringat Jetty. Island jetty infrastructure is being renewed now — a natural window to plan the next-generation service that will use it.

first_electric_ferry.headline: Singapore's first fully electric ferry already runs daily.
first_electric_ferry.detail: Penguin-built 200-passenger electric ferry for Shell: Pasir Panjang Ferry Terminal <-> Pulau Bukom, 5.5 km in ~12 minutes; service sized to carry >3,000 passengers/day at maturity (launched May 2023).
first_electric_ferry.relevance: Electric passenger service in Singapore port waters is proven practice, not a concept.

green_initiative.name: Maritime Singapore Green Initiative
green_initiative.detail: MPA pledged up to S$100M; green incentives refreshed 2024, incl. port-dues reductions tied to clean harbour craft.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the clean-harbour-craft standard MPA's 2030 mandate is reaching for. Foiling cuts energy per passenger-mile dramatically, so electric range and speed both work; it is near-silent and low-wake in a dense, busy port; and the Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer cross-border legs with no charging dependency. Singapore is the ideal jurisdiction to prove it first-of-class and export the benchmark — starting with the domestic harbour and Southern-Islands network, with cross-border relief corridors as an optional second step.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real berths/jetties during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Several are LIVE ferry stops today (Marina South Pier, Changi Point, the Southern Islands); Marina South Pier is also the e-HC charging pilot site.

boarding_points.name: Marina Bay water-taxi stops (Esplanade / Bayfront / Promontory)

domestic_pairs.rationale: A fast foiling commuter line from the East Coast straight up to the Marina Bay/CBD water-taxi stops — new capacity for a land-constrained city. Anchor commuter corridor.
Inner-harbour hop from Marina Bay/CBD to Keppel Bay / HarbourFront along the southern waterfront.
Marina South Pier to St John's / Lazarus — a live Southern-Islands ferry corridor today, foiling-upgraded. Marina South Pier is the e-HC charging pilot site.
Marina South Pier to Kusu Island — live Southern-Islands ferry corridor.
Sentosa Cove to the Southern Islands — short inner-harbour leisure/island hop.
Changi Point to Pulau Ubin — a live bumboat corridor today; a clean foiling upgrade to an existing island link.
Working-waterfront run from the West Coast / Pasir Panjang to HarbourFront.
Jurong Island industrial waterfront to HarbourFront along the working harbour.

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. All are live ferry corridors today or recognized congestion-relief surfaces. None leads the proposal.

links.note: Singapore (Tanah Merah) <-> Batam is a live ferry corridor with millions of crossings yearly. Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal is the real cross-border berth; routed across the Singapore Strait. Pioneer/Quanta range.
Singapore (Tanah Merah) <-> Bintan (Bandar Bentan Telani); 350k+ tourists/yr. Quanta-LR range across the Strait.
Singapore <-> Johor/Desaru as a Causeway-relief surface; subject to bilateral operating review. Routing must go around the island ends of the Johor Strait, never through/over the Causeway.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings. The Port of Singapore is one of the world's busiest — foiling must use cleared corridors with geofenced low-wake/no-foil zones in anchorages and fairways. Hand-curated waypoints required throughout.

hazards.hazard: Port anchorages & fairways / Traffic Separation Scheme
hazards.detail: The harbour and Singapore Strait carry heavy commercial traffic, anchorages and a Traffic Separation Scheme. Route on cleared corridors; cross fairways and the TSS only at marked points; geofence low-wake/no-foil zones in anchorages with full pilotage compliance.

The Causeway physically blocks the middle of the Johor Strait. Any Singapore<->Johor/Desaru leg must route AROUND the eastern (Tebrau Strait) or western end of the island — never through or over the Causeway embankment.

hazards.hazard: Sisters' Islands Marine Park & Southern reefs
hazards.detail: The Southern Islands are reef-fringed (Sisters' Islands is a protected marine park). Keep clear of reef flats, no-wake on approach, snap entries to charted channels.
Avoid Pulau Tekong and the eastern live-firing/danger areas entirely; route the Changi<->Ubin leg through the charted Serangoon Harbour channel.

Cross-border legs cross the Singapore Strait shipping lanes; cross the TSS at right angles at marked points and snap the Indonesian approaches (Batam Centre, Bandar Bentan Telani) to their real ferry berths.

hazards.hazard: Live-firing islands west of the Southern Islands (Pulau Sudong, Pulau Senang, Pulau Pawai)
hazards.detail: Proclaimed SAF manoeuvring and live-firing grounds incl. surrounding waters; public must keep clear (MINDEF advisories). No route may approach these islands; keep all Southern-Islands legs east of the firing-ground boundary.

St John's Island jetty and Kusu bumboat jetty under repair; current public landings consolidate at Lazarus Pulau Seringat Jetty and Kusu main jetty. Bind boarding points to jetties verified open at service start.
